restrictions: Target sha256-r37-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..36 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is verified with the target before it is returned.

Algorithm: the two-block attack of Li, Zhang, Li, Liu, Qian and Zhu (IACR ePrint 2026/1120) with its 37-step characteristic and Step-1 solution S (6c77089c), the 222 largest classes of A0-variants of S (782,800 variants; 1c368173, b947b377, 1f12a09a), each class base | s for s in one of ten lists whose free bits 0, 2, 3 (or 0) form a cube (Sections 5.3, 8.1), and the packed good-pair stage of 0db0eeb6; as in ffbe30bb the eight value bits E18[1,5,10,11,18,28,29], E19[29] are not imposed (four patterns, Section 7.6); as in ad06162f (R16x), E16[23] = 0 and E16[24] = E17[24] are not imposed (Section 7.4c); as in 96169e7c, scan_table is at word address 0 and Ul/Um are 4-lane packed in 5 primitives (Sections 9.3, 9.6-9.8); the bit-sliced algebra (W6_OPS 181..301, SUBF_OPS 11..28, F7_OPS 112) is that of d9f8833d and fd115760, carried over here (Sections 8, 9.5). No table is indexed by x = A_{-1}: bit-sliced W7/W6 tests, packed row-16 address, two 4096-word chunk tables, exact test, then rows 16..36.

Cost: fixed caps N_FB = 60539782602738506 first blocks (2^55.74873; each one target compression plus 514 counted operations) and V_MAX = 1681620533283028982309 counted data-dependent operations (halt when exceeded), with calibrated A_C = 2^48 (characteristic and SFS-pair search; > 169x the 593,858 solver CPU-seconds = 2^40.61 units measured for the 35-step search in 6eeefb64; sensitivity at A_C = 2^56, 2^60, 2^64 in proof.md Section 12), A_S = 2^50 (Step-1 SAT solve), DEV = 2^40 (development) and 2^38 operations of preprocessing (Section 14.2): 2^59.300050 target compressions on every run (Section 11), claimed 59.30006. Every target compression is charged one unit; every executed load, store, logic operation, shift, addition (address additions included), comparison and branch is one primitive, the plane programs counted by an algebra with static constants and inversion flags (Section 9.1); there is no decision-DAG pricing.

Success probability at least 0.39 (0.3900000053) under H1 (independent uniform chaining values of the first blocks), H2 (q3 >= 2^-71.4629 with the four row-18/19 value patterns and R16x (E16[23] = 0 and E16[24] = E17[24] not imposed) accepted jointly: the lower, rounded down to four decimals, of the one-sided 99 percent bounds 2^-71.4629 and 2^-71.4524 of two preregistered blocks of 128 replicates of a sequential Monte-Carlo estimator written for this filing, proof.md Section 7.4c and Appendix G; the same program with Table 15's cells reproduces the registered study of 7319bba), H3 (given one success, at most 2^-9.4 further successes expected in the same first block; stated as our theory with organizer experiments, Appendix H) and H7, by a per-first-block Bonferroni bound and independence across first blocks; Bernstein's inequality bounds the work-cap overflow (cap slack 1/24000) below 0.00000019. No expected-work bound and no independence-of-conditions model is used.

Memory: all tables, the code and the constants occupy 935,612 bytes = 2^19.84 (proof.md Section 14.1), below 2^20 bytes. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score. The per-first-block counts of the ledger are exact expectations or stated bounds on them (proof.md Section 11.1); the simulation of proof.md Section 13.3 on real first blocks is a check and is not used in the ledger.

heuristics.statement: Our theory: the first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings; their chaining values CV1 = F_37(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values; in particular x = A_{-1} is uniform on 2^32 and independent of cb = C6 - A_{-2}, which is uniform on 2^32. Consequences used: each of the 222 classes passes the W7 test with probability p7 = |F7|/2^32 exactly, each variant of a passing class then passes F6 with probability p6 = |F6|/2^32 exactly, and given both, W0..W5 are uniform and independent of (W6, W7) (proof.md Lemma 5.1); hence the expected number of good pairs per first block is g = 782,800 p7 p6 = 830.988, the expected counts of the ledger, and the independence of distinct first blocks.
heuristics.scope: The expected numbers of passing classes, good pairs, survivors and row-16 passes per first block; the expected operation count of the counted program; the law of the second-block words that defines q3; independence across first blocks (proof.md Section 10). Not the validity of any output: every output is verified with the target.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured by 7319bba with the attack's own filters on real first blocks in C (2^21 and 2^23 first blocks: passing classes 7,400,134 and 29,545,568 against 7,388,160 and 29,552,640 expected; good pairs ratio 1.0034 and 1.0011; row-16 pairs z = +0.88, +0.51), by this filing's simulation of the counted program on 20,000 real first blocks (passing classes per first block 3.457 against the exact 3.523, good pairs 836.3 against 831.0, mean counted operations 28377 against the ledger's 28290), by the unconditional sample in a0-online-r37 (64 organizer-seeded first blocks per active trial: 90,682 class W7 passes in 25,600 first blocks of our 400-trial run against 90,187 expected), and by the organizer experiment h1-cv1-filters-nonce, which counts on 150 organizer-seeded real first blocks per trial how often the W7 filter (first class) and the W6 filter (its first four variants) pass (expected 2.38 and 40.1 per trial; our replays, 100 trials each: 244 and 214 W7 passes against 238.0, 4,011 and 3,988 W6 passes against 4,013.7; Appendix H). These are at most 2^23 real first blocks, not 2^55.8.
heuristics.limitations: Premise (our theory), not a theorem: the filter rates are measured on at most 2^23 real first blocks and on the organizer's small samples, not at the 2^55.8 first blocks of the attack, and independence across first blocks is assumed, not tested. The class tests of one first block are strongly correlated (their c7 values are close), so per-first-block counts are overdispersed; only their expectations and the independence across first blocks are used. The class test uses the single word x, so H1 is also an assumption about that word of the digest of a 37-step compression.

heuristics.statement: For a good pair, q3 = the average over the 782,800 variants of the 222 classes (each equally likely, as examined here) and the 32 elements of L* of Pr[rows 16..36 of both members follow every cell and every printed two-bit condition closing at rows >= 16 (corrected reading A15[29] = A17[29]), the eight value bits E18[1,5,10,11,18,28,29] and E19[29] of Table 15 not imposed, and (R16x) E16[23] = 0 and E16[24] = E17[24] not imposed: exactly the cells and conditions of experiments/lowm.py] satisfies q3_used = 2^-71.4629 <= q3 <= 2^-71.38 < 2^-70, where 2^-71.4629 is the lower, rounded down to four decimals of log2 (the preregistered rule's two decimals give 2^-71.47 and a claim of 59.30714), of the one-sided 99 percent Student lower bounds (2^-71.4629 and 2^-71.4524; one-sided 99 percent upper bounds 2^-71.3970 and 2^-71.3838) of the means of two preregistered blocks of 128 replicates (NP = 8192) of a sequential Monte-Carlo estimator written for this filing (Appendices F and G), run on exactly this family with both relaxations as one carrier; this heuristic explicitly includes the statistical and procedural premise that the participant-reported preregistrations, complete contiguous seed lists (710000..710063, 720000..720127, 721000..721127, 740000..740127, 741000..741127), fixed two-block min(LB) rule, interim progress monitoring during execution, and prior condition-relaxation screening (adopting the four row-18/19 patterns and R16x after screening 30 candidate condition pairs) do not introduce selection, optional-stopping, or multiple-comparison bias exceeding the margin between the two disjoint-seed block estimates, the 6-seed direct full-path check and the declared floor q3_used = 2^-71.4629.
heuristics.scope: The expected number of successes E[X] = N_FB g 32 q3 and hence N_FB (proof.md Sections 7 and 10), including the validity of the offline SMC estimation protocol, seed selection, stopping rule, and relaxation screening that support q3_used = 2^-71.4629. The good pairs and the later rows are those of 7319bba; this filing changes how the good pairs are found, not which pairs are good, and which pairs count as a success: (from ffbe30bb) the value patterns of rows 18 and 19 and (new) R16x at rows 16 and 17, which also gives the four l = 0, 2, 16, 18 row-16 values.
heuristics.extrapolation: Lemma 7.1: rows 16..22 have exactly the same probability for every variant; a variant enters rows >= 23 only through W8 in W23 and W24, so only the four W24 conditions can depend on it (about 2^-4 for every W8x). Our estimator (exact row 16, exact importance weights at rows 17..21, (W6, W7) uniform on F6 x F7, W8 drawn uniformly from the 782,800 variants; Appendix F) was preregistered (validation V with Table 15 cells: mean 2^-73.9911, bound 2^-74.0064, z = +0.66 against the registered study B of 7319bba, mean 2^-73.9987, bound 2^-74.0225, validation PASSES both preregistered criteria (|z| <= 2.576; bound within 0.04 of -74.0225); main blocks R1 and R2 with the eight value characters of the two E cells removed: means 2^-71.9975 and 2^-71.9868, relative sd 0.0714 and 0.0681, bounds 2^-72.0191 and 2^-72.0074, declared 2^-72.02; stage factors of rows 18, 19 and 21 -8.00, -10.00 and -2.00 bits against -15.00, -6.00 and -1.00 for Table 15, structural gain 2.00) and again with R16x (constants written from the counted program; the same binary reproduces the four-pattern outputs byte for byte; joint blocks J1 and J2: means 2^-71.4296 and 2^-71.4177, relative sd 0.1096 and 0.1143, lower bounds 2^-71.4629 and 2^-71.4524, upper bounds 2^-71.3970 and 2^-71.3838, 0.55 bits above the four patterns alone; our earlier full-path test of R16x with independent rehash of all 30,814 collisions gave +0.590 bit [0.548, 0.631]). In addition, the organizer experiment a0-sfs-r37 constructs and verifies full 37-step SFS collisions across 128 classes and all 8 pattern branches (63/64 on patterns 0..3 and 57/64 on R16x patterns 4..7 on our seeds ours-A-0..127; 13 of 13 returned pairs of trials 0..15 are found by the counted program), and the organizer experiment h3-ladder-r37 runs the row-16 stage of q3 on organizer seeds: 41 exact row-16 passes among 98,216 W6 passes (4.2e-4, two seed sets) against the 4.9e-4 (2^-11) per probed lane of the ledger (Appendix H). The four-pattern relaxation (exactly four feasible patterns, three verified further collisions) is ffbe30bb's; here the three collisions are re-checked against this package's cells. R16x is ours (each of its two conditions alone is necessary; a sweep of 30 further condition pairs found no further gain). Here the examined law is the studied law (every variant of every passing class, no weighting), so no hedge is added. With q3 one bit lower the claim would be 60.29862 (61.15687 under A_C = 2^60), with the four patterns alone (2^-72.02) 59.85624 (60.92973 under A_C = 2^60) and with the Table 15 value 2^-74.03 61.86477 (62.21470 under A_C = 2^60).
heuristics.limitations: A Monte-Carlo and procedural premise, not a theorem: (1) its coverage rests on the approximate normality of the mean of 128 replicates (relative sd 0.1096 and 0.1143, about twice the Table 15 study's because few children survive the row-19 stage); row-22 survivors are heavily duplicated within a replicate; the row-22 stage draws (W6, W7) uniformly from F6 x F7, which is argued, not measured; depends on the reading of the '+' cells; (2) the offline preregistration timestamps/hashes (PREREG_q3M.txt, PREREG_q3R16x.txt) and contiguous seed lists (710000..710063, 720000..720127, 721000..721127, 740000..740127, 741000..741127) are participant-reported without an organizer holdout nonce, interim progress looks were taken while blocks ran (Appendices F.2 and G.2), and screening R16x against 30 other condition pairs before running J1 and J2 is not a multiplicity-adjusted holdout test, so the absence of material selection, optional-stopping, or multiple-testing bias is an explicit part of heuristic H2 rather than an externally certified guarantee; (3) no organizer experiment executes the end event of q3: rows 22..36 reach the digest only through a second-block chaining value that must be equal, which needs a reachable first block, that is the attack itself (a0-sfs-r37 returns semi-free-start pairs and no full collision of the target); the organizer-executed h3-ladder-r37 runs only the row-16 stage of q3 on organizer seeds. Premise (our theory): q3 is our computation, with the estimator, the preregistrations and the per-seed estimates printed in Appendices F and G. The count of four patterns is a solver enumeration (Bitwuzla; Z3 on smaller cases) for the published dense part with the signed cells of rows 14 and 15 kept (with rows 12..15 removed as well it admits 128 patterns); other dense parts were not explored, and our estimator does not use the solver. R16x has no solver enumeration: its value rests on the estimator, on a0-sfs-r37, and on our full-path test with rehashed collisions; patterns of rows 16..21 outside the program's cells (for example the E18 XOR pattern {24,23,16,15}) are not counted. A stated premise, not an established fact.

heuristics.statement: Averaged over the trials t = (first block, variant, l) of a first block f weighted by their success probabilities, the expected number of other successful trials of the same first block given that t succeeds is at most 2^-9.4: sum_t Pr[A_t] E[X_f - 1 | A_t] <= 2^-9.4 E[X_f]. Equivalently: (a) the expected number of other l in L* succeeding with the same variant is at most 2^-11, and (b) for other good pairs t' of the same first block, Pr[t' succeeds | t succeeds, t' good] <= 2^35 Pr[t' succeeds | t' good].
heuristics.scope: The per-first-block Bonferroni bound Pr[X_f >= 1] >= (1 - 2^-10.4) E[X_f] (proof.md Section 10). The good pairs of a first block and their dependence structure are those of 7319bba; this filing changes the order in which they are processed, not the set.
heuristics.extrapolation: (a) 7319bba's replay of 19,620,436 distinct Step-3 successes of the SMC: rebuilding W0..W5 and testing the other 31 elements of L* through rows 14..36 gave 0 further successes (rule-of-three 95 percent bound 2^-22.65 per success; the accepted patterns raise the chance of passing rows 18 and 19 by about 4 and R16x the chance of the whole path by about 1.6, with four more l holding row 16, so about 2^-19.8, far below 2^-11; in that replay the other l fail at row 16 or 17). (b) Summing over all other trials t' = (f, a0', l') in the family uses the family average of Pr[t' succeeds | t' good], which is q3 <= 2^-71.38 < 2^-70 (H2; no per-trial uniformity across (a0, l) is required), so the expected number of further successes among other good pairs is at most rho x N_good x 32 x q3 with N_good <= 782,800 (all variants of the family): 2^35 x 2^19.58 x 2^5 x 2^-70 = 2^-10.42, so delta <= 2^-11 + 2^-10.42 < 2^-9.4; the measured factor at the row-16 level over 2^21 and 2^23 real first blocks is 0.98 and 1.00. The organizer experiment h3-cowpass-nonce counts the first blocks in which several variants of one class pass F6 together, and h3-ladder-r37 (Appendix H) counts, on organizer-seeded real first blocks, the pairs of distinct variants of one first block that both pass each level of the attack through the exact row-16 test, against the pairs expected if they passed independently: our replays (two seed sets) give the dependence factor 3.62 and 4.92 at the W6 filter (variants of one class share bits), 0.99 and 1.00 and 0.95 and 0.94 at the two table levels, and 1.27 and 0.67 at the exact row-16 test (32 and 9 passes). This is the bound of the earlier filings on this family; the whole family G would give 2^-6.5 and is not used.
heuristics.limitations: Premise (our theory): rows 17..36 are not reachable by any organizer experiment of 20 s; for them rho = 2^35 over the measured factor (0.67 to 1.27 through row 16 on organizer seeds; 0.98 and 1.00 over 2^21 and 2^23 real first blocks) is the stated allowance. Rows >= 17 of distinct good pairs cannot be measured jointly within one first block; the premise leaves a margin of 2^35 over the measured row-16 factor, and the margin over the number of examined pairs is thin (delta <= 2^-9.68 against 2^-9.4). The replay samples are correlated through SMC resampling. A stated premise, not an established fact.

heuristics.statement: The published characteristic, its two-bit conditions, the SFS pair's inner values S and L* are used as advice. Their construction is charged A_S = 2^50 (the Step-1 SAT solve, reported by the paper at 2^41.3, and the completion of a Step-1 solution to the SFS pair) and calibrated A_C = 2^48 (the unpublished characteristic search, > 169 times the 593,858 solver CPU-seconds = 2^40.61 units measured for the predecessor 35-step search in 6eeefb64; sensitivity at A_C = 2^56, 2^60, 2^64 is reported in proof.md Section 12); all development computation at DEV = 2^40. The variant family, the 222 class descriptors (below 2^13 bytes), the lists, the filter sets, L* and the tables are recomputed in the preprocessing (2^38 operations bound, itemised in proof.md Section 14.2).
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (2^50.32305) and the advice (below 2^13 bytes).
heuristics.extrapolation: proof.md Section 11.2. A_S: 2^8.7 times the paper's reported Step-1 cost; the completion of a Step-1 solution to a full 37-step semi-free-start pair is reproduced in this package in about 25 milliseconds per pair (organizer experiment a0-sfs-r37). A_C: at the CPU-second price calibrated in the accepted filing 6eeefb64 (2^21.427 units at C = 2644 per solver CPU-second), A_C = 2^48 units is 2^26.57 solver CPU-seconds (~3.17 core-years), > 169 times (2^7.39x) the 593,858 solver CPU-seconds (2^40.61 units) that filing charged as a measured complete re-run of the predecessor 35-step search; we also report sensitivity across the full unamortized allowance spectrum: A_C = 2^56 gives time_log2 = 59.43904, A_C = 2^60 gives 60.69185, and A_C = 2^64 gives 64.05445.
heuristics.limitations: The 37-step characteristic search time is unpublished; A_C = 2^48 is calibrated with a 2^7.39x factor above the accepted measurement of the predecessor 35-step search (593,858 solver CPU-seconds = 2^40.61 units in 6eeefb64), not a direct measurement of the paper's search. A_C = 2^56 would give time_log2 = 59.43904, A_C = 2^60 would give 60.69185, and A_C = 2^64 would give 64.05445.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5 a word-RAM program of 256-bit primitives in which every executed load, store, logic operation, shift, addition, comparison, branch and jump is one primitive is charged by the primitives it executes. The W7 class test (112 primitives for all 222 classes) and the W6 test of a batch of 256 reps (181 to 301 primitives, and 11 to 28 for each subtraction run) are straight-line plane programs whose counts do not depend on the data, produced by a plane algebra in which static constants fold and complemented planes carry an inversion flag at no cost, and in which a NOT is paid when an AND or OR meets unequal flags; two batches are processed together bit by bit with at most 20 live planes each (64 registers, no spill). The group of four members is 31 primitives, the probe of a group (11, 8, 8, 6) = 33 primitives via 4-lane packed Ul and Um chunk-table addresses, the exact row-16 test 34, and the zero-base scan_table at word address 0 prices CLS_LANE = 5, SCAN_LANE = 7 and SURV_LANE = 6, with the scalar and control items of proof.md Section 9. All tables, the code (bounded by 2^16 bytes) and the constants occupy 935,612 bytes = 2^19.84, below 2^20 bytes. The 222 classes are base | s for s in ten lists (computed, checked for all 782,800 variants); a list is the union of 2^|B| translates of its reps by the cube B of free bits {0, 2, 3} or {0}, and F6(W6x) does not depend on a cube bit s_b when q_b = 1 or on s_0 when CB3_0 = 1 (Lemma 8.2: proved from the constants of S and checked), which the program uses to run only the main combination and subtract the constants of the other 2^|Q0| - 1 combinations that matter.
heuristics.scope: The class-test, W6, scan, gather, group, probe and survivor terms of the ledger (essentially all of the 27775.96 data-dependent operations per first block), the fixed terms, the memory figure and the preprocessing bound (2^38 operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: The program is experiments/lowm.py (the plane programs assert their counts at every execution; process_cv counts every scalar item where it executes; the realized operation count of every category equals its closed formula on 20,000 simulated first blocks). It is exact against the scalar definitions: every lane of every class-test plane and every pass plane equals the F7 or F6 test of its definition (44,400 and 39,894 lanes in selftest, and every lane of every processed class in a0-online-r37), the sets of good pairs (all members, after the expansion of the reps) equal the brute-force sets, the address u equals W0 + s0(W1) from the step equations, the exact row-16 test equals the enumeration of 2,097,152 pairs on all 32 l (Appendix A) and the generic row check on random and near-miss values, and the table stage never rejects a member.
heuristics.limitations: No organizer ruling is cited for the plane algebra (static constants and inversion flags are compile-time facts of the text; the W6 programs have 32 to 84 inversion flips that cost nothing because XORs absorb them and AND/OR of equally flagged planes use De Morgan; pricing every one of them as a NOT would give 59.33912, or 60.70686 under A_C = 2^60) or for the register argument, which is a count of live planes, not a register allocation. The code size is a bound (at most 8192 primitives of at most 8 bytes). Branch pricing follows the earlier filings (a branch on a register is one primitive). The ceiling of the group count and the survivor scan are charged at their worst case (below 0.2 percent of the data-dependent work).

heuristics.statement: The cap target is mu0 = 0.49466274, the smallest 8-decimal number strictly above -ln(0.61 - Pcap - 2^-60) / (1 - 2^-10.4) with Pcap = 0.00000019 the assumed bound of the Bernstein work-cap failure probability. With E[X] >= mu0 the success bound of proof.md Section 10, 1 - exp(-(1 - 2^-10.4) mu0) - Pcap - 2^-60, is >= 0.39000000 with no further padding.
heuristics.extrapolation: Every allowance is an explicit term of the floor equation: the Bernstein cap-failure bound Pcap (priced in proof.md Section 10 from the exact vmax_fb and vbar of the ledger; the computed bound is 2^-22.39), the repeated-first-block allowance 2^-60, and the H3 dependence discount as the divisor (1 - 2^-10.4). Appendix C computes mu0 and the bound with 60-digit decimals and asserts the bound > 0.39; lowm.py ledger() iterates Pcap and N_FB to a fixed point and asserts the same.
heuristics.limitations: The 0.39 floor is the organizer's success requirement; the equation makes the success arithmetic exact rather than adding slack. The cap bound needs the independence of the first blocks (H1) and the bound vmax_fb on one first block's work; a Chebyshev bound would give the slack 2^-11 and 59.30883 (Section 10).
